name: marketing-buttons
title: Buttons
description: Marketing-focused button styles for landing pages and promotional sites, including solid, bordered, icon-adorned, icon-bubble CTA, and quiet text/underline variants optimized for conversion-oriented contexts.
useWhen: Building CTAs for landing pages, hero sections, or promotional banners where visual impact matters.
Pairing a primary solid button with a secondary bordered or text button to establish action hierarchy.
Using icon-adorned buttons to reinforce the action (download arrow, forward arrow) in hero sections.
avoidWhen: Building form submission buttons inside application forms — use application button styles instead.
The action is a navigation link within body text — use an inline <a> link rather than a button element.
More than two buttons appear side-by-side at the same visual weight — establish hierarchy with solid + ghost pairing.
responsiveBehavior: Button groups stack vertically on small screens. Pill-shaped buttons maintain their border-radius at all widths. Icon-bubble CTA buttons reduce their icon bubble size on mobile.
accessibility: Use <button> for actions and <a> for navigation — do not interchange them.
Icon-only buttons must have an aria-label describing the action.
Ensure button text and background meet WCAG AA contrast in all states (default, hover, focus, disabled).

variants.title: Solid and bordered
variants.description: Paired solid primary and outlined secondary pill buttons — the standard two-button CTA combination for landing page hero sections.
accessibility: Primary and secondary buttons must both have descriptive labels; focus ring must be visible on both.

variants.title: Solid and bordered (Dark)
variants.description: Solid-and-bordered button pair adapted for dark landing page surfaces with inverted colors.
accessibility: Button text and background must meet WCAG AA contrast in both solid and bordered variants on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Solid and bordered with icon
variants.description: CTA button pair with a leading or trailing icon reinforcing the action — download arrow, chevron, or app-store logo alongside the label.
accessibility: Icons inside labeled buttons are decorative; set aria-hidden='true' on icon elements.

variants.title: Solid and bordered with icon (Dark)
variants.description: Icon-adorned CTA button pair adapted for dark marketing surfaces.
accessibility: Icon and label colors must meet contrast requirements on dark button backgrounds.

variants.title: Icon only, solid and bordered
variants.description: Compact circular icon-only buttons for toolbar actions, social links, or floating action buttons in marketing UI.
accessibility: Icon-only buttons require an aria-label describing the action since there is no visible text label.

variants.title: Icon only, solid and bordered (Dark)
variants.description: Circular icon-only buttons adapted for dark marketing surfaces.
accessibility: Icon fill must meet contrast requirements against both solid and bordered button backgrounds on dark surfaces.

variants.title: CTA with icon bubble
variants.description: High-impact CTA button with a framed icon bubble on one side — a distinctive pattern used in SaaS hero sections and product launch pages.
accessibility: Icon bubble is decorative when the button label describes the action; icon element should be aria-hidden.

variants.title: CTA with icon bubble (Dark)
variants.description: Icon-bubble CTA button adapted for dark hero sections and promotional blocks.
accessibility: Icon bubble and label text must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark button backgrounds.

variants.title: Quiet text and underline buttons
variants.description: Lightweight text-only and underline-style buttons for secondary actions, 'Learn more' links, and de-emphasized CTAs within content sections.
accessibility: Underline distinguishes these from plain body text; ensure focus state is clearly visible on quiet buttons.

variants.title: Quiet text and underline buttons (Dark)
variants.description: Quiet text and underline CTA buttons adapted for dark marketing surfaces.
accessibility: Quiet button text and underline color must meet contrast requirements against dark page backgrounds.
